chunks: From Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Naqash al-Qummi, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nakhas narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Rummani narrated to us, saying: Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Tayalisi narrated to us, from Mukhtar al-Tammari, from Abu Mattar, who said:

When the impious Ibn Muljam struck the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Shall I kill him?' He said: 'No, but detain him. When I die, kill him. And when I die, bury me in this elevation, in the grave of my two brothers, Hud and Salih (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.ابْنُ مُلْجَمٍ: Ibn Muljam (Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Hudhayl), the killer of Imam Ali
key_terms.الظَّهْرِ: The elevation or high ground, referring to a specific location in Kufa
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُ: The impious one, a title often used for Ibn Muljam
key_terms.هُودٍ وَصَالِحٍ: Hud and Salih, two prophets whose graves are traditionally associated with this location

ai.seo_question: What were Imam Ali's instructions regarding the burial of his body and the killing of Ibn Muljam?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s deliberate choice to delay the execution of Ibn Muljam to avoid the people attributing his death to a political assassination rather than divine decree, a key theme in Shia historiography. The instruction to be buried in 'this elevation' (*dhahar*) among the graves of prophets Hud and Salih underscores the continuity of prophetic lineage and the sanctity of Kufa, while the specific mention of these prophets connects Ali’s martyrdom to the broader narrative of divine messengers. This event is central to understanding the ritual practices of visiting the grave of Imam Ali and the theological significance of his burial site in the Masjid al-Kufa.
